newsitem.title: USA: Newhall sees surpassing 30 pct revs rise.
newsitem.headline: Newhall sees surpassing 30 pct revs rise.

text.p: The Newhall Land and Farming company said that despite lower revenues and earnings for the third quarter compared with the same quarter last year it expected to exceed its previously stated average annual earnings growth goal of more than 30 percent for the full year 1996 over 1995.

The company said, "All major aspects of our three business segments -- residential, commercial and industrial -- continue to be strong and we expect to exceed our long-term goal of 30 percent average annual earnings growth in the full year 1996.

Earnings for the first nine months are 20 percent ahead of the total for 1995 and 24 percent ahead on a per-unit basis due to the reduction in partnership units outstanding as a result of the company's repurchase program. Since 1995, Newhall Land has repurchased 4.4 percent of the total units then outstanding." For the quarter ended Sept. 30, 1996, revenues were $39.2 million vs. $43.2 million a year ago. Net income was $4.2 million, or 12 cents per partnership unit, compared with $6.3 million, or 18 cents per unit, in the third quarter last year. Included in the 1995 third quarter results was the sale of 5,501 acres of the Merced Ranch, which added $7.4 million to revenues and $4.6 million, or 13 cents per unit, to operating income.

The company said its portfolio of income-producing properties continues to expand through its active development program. When projects started in 1995, 1996 and 1997 are operational, Newhall Land will more than double the value of the portfolio, which was $280 million at the end of 1994. These projects are expected to add $320 million to the portfolio's value, before deducting for project debt. For the quarter ended Sept. 30, 1996, income from commercial operations, which include Valencia Water Company, Newhall Land's wholly owned public water utility, increased slightly from 1995 due to improved results from the water company. For the first nine months of 1996, revenues and income from the commercial portfolio were slightly below year-earlier results due to the 1995 sale of the ITT building and Bouquet Shopping Center. The company said it expects 1996 results from the portfolio to be about 10 percent below 1995 since projects started in 1995 "will not contribute meaningful revenues and income until 1997."
